headline: 🔍 1709 FIELDSTONE'S INSPECTION HAS A DATE AND THE BUYER SIDE IS WAITING ON YOU — their inspector's earliest is THURSDAY 8/13, the ask landed at 2:35 this afternoon and no answer has gone back. Meanwhile 355 Comanche has two showings booked this weekend and BOTH of its 'interested: YES' agents now have names, neither of whom was ever told the price came down.

hotSignals.signal: Robert B. at RealtyCore wrote at 2:35 PM that the earliest day his inspector had was Thursday and asked whether that works on your end, with the time still to be worked out — nine hours after his buyers returned the initialed contract.
hotSignals.action: Answer Thursday 8/13 today. It is one sentence, and it is the SECOND unanswered written question from this agent in two days — his Friday close-date ask is still the last message in its thread past thirty hours. Both were overtaken by events rather than replied to.

hotSignals.signal: Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage answered 'interested: Yes' and wrote "Writing up an offer!" on her form while calling $299,000 too high — and that is the offer you confirmed dead this morning, from a buyer who was never told the price came down to $295,000.
hotSignals.action: CALL HER — thank her for showing, tell her the number her client called too high is now $295,000, and ask what gets their buyer in the house. Quote $295,000 and nothing else. No email — a buyer's agent on a live listing is a call, not a message. ⚠️ Her written read has now aged out of the 14-day window; the call task is live and the signal is carried here deliberately rather than dropped.

hotSignals.signal: Angela B. at Keller Williams Vestavia filed the listing's other 'interested: Yes', objecting only to the price at $299,000 and noting her buyer had seen another home she liked.
hotSignals.action: Call her — the price objection has already been answered by the 8/5 reduction and she was never told. Six days on, the cross-shopped house is either under contract or not, and one call settles it. Quote $295,000 only.

hotSignals.signal: Mallory W. at ARC Realty filed the only unqualified 'interested: Yes / priced just right' this board has ever taken.
hotSignals.action: The agent call is cleared. The open item is the seller decision behind it — one call covers this seller's three files.

An agent who thinks a house is overpriced usually says so; this one declined to say anything at all.

🔎 THE ANONYMOUS ROW, NAMED YESTERDAY MORNING. Interested: YES. Priced TOO HIGH against the $299,000 list. Staging 4 of 5 — the best staging score this listing has ever taken, and it undercuts the theory that presentation is the whole problem. ⭐ HER FREE TEXT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: "Saw another home that she is interested in." That is a cross-shopping buyer, not a rejection — and her price objection was answered three days later by the cut to $295,000, which she was never told about. ⚠️ Like every other agent on this file, she left 'what price' blank.

🔥 NOT A FEEDBACK FORM — A DEAL. At 9:05 Friday morning he wrote that the buyers agree to ALL of the counter's new terms with one exception: they want to close on or before Oct 23 rather than Oct 30, because they have four kids and moving the week of Halloween will not work. ⭐ Price agreed. Concession agreed. Co-op agreed. Stated as ABSENCE, not failure: a phone call leaves no trace here.
🔥 WROTE THE OFFER. Contract, pre-approval letter and a personal letter from the buyers, submitted 3:15 PM, followed by his own text eleven minutes later.
